halfLife.notes: Very long half-life — natural slow washout on stopping. Steady state in ~2 weeks. Once-daily dosing. Long half-life reduces discontinuation syndrome risk compared with SSRIs/SNRIs. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

activeMetabolite.notes: No clinically significant active metabolites. Parent compound accounts for activity.

cypInteractions.switchingRelevance: Strong CYP2D6 inhibitors (paroxetine, fluoxetine, bupropion) roughly double vortioxetine exposure — reduce vortioxetine dose by 50% if co-prescribed. CYP2D6 inducers (rifampicin, carbamazepine) halve exposure. The fluoxetine–vortioxetine interaction is bidirectional: fluoxetine's CYP2D6 inhibition and fluoxetine's own serotonergic activity both complicate the cross-taper. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

maoiWashout.notes: 14-day washout from vortioxetine before any MAOI. 14 days off any MAOI before starting vortioxetine. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

discontinuationSyndromeRisk.notes: Very long half-life provides a natural self-taper. Discontinuation syndrome is uncommon and generally mild. Abrupt cessation is less problematic than with SSRIs or SNRIs. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

formulationNotes: Start at 10 mg in most patients. Titrate to 20 mg if tolerated and response inadequate. Reduce to 5 mg if 10 mg not tolerated. Note: cognitive benefits and antidepressant effect may have a dose-response relationship. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.
specialConsiderations: Cognitive benefits (verbal memory, processing speed) are a differentiating feature — particularly useful in patients with residual cognitive impairment.
Nausea is the most common early side effect — counsel to take with food, usually resolves in 1–2 weeks.
CYP2D6 poor metabolisers achieve 2× higher exposure — start at 5 mg in this population.
